value.body: Keeps an organisation's computers, networks, email and software working — setting up machines, fixing problems raised by staff, managing user accounts and escalating harder issues. IT support engineers work in IT services and managed-services firms, company IT teams, help desks and data centres. A typical day is spent working through a ticket queue on calls, in remote sessions or at desks.

items.label: Typical entry
items.note: Diploma holders also enter service-desk roles

items.label: Common tools
items.value: Windows and Linux, directory services, ticketing systems, remote-desktop tools

items.label: Indian tech-sector workforce
items.note: Whole IT-BPM sector, not this role alone

value.title: How you get in
value.body: Many freshers enter through campus or walk-in hiring for L1 support or service-desk roles at IT services and managed-services firms, often with rotational shifts. Basic networking, operating-system troubleshooting and clear spoken communication are what interviews check. An entry-level networking or cloud certification can help.

value.title: Skills you'll use
items: Networking basics — IP, DNS, Wi-Fi, VPN

value.title: At a glance
items: Shift work, including nights and weekends, is common in support roles.
Growth path: L1 → L2/L3 support → system or network administrator → cloud or security roles.
Routine tasks are increasingly automated, so scripting and cloud skills matter for the long term.
